ASSURANCE / INDEPENDENT TOPIC

Ready for other languages and locales?

An independent saga for locale policy, localisable content, language review and locale journeys.

The current assessment covers five homepage entry routes. Levels describe evidence maturity within that scope; every topic keeps its own requirements and open work.

Internationalisation

Level 1 — Scoped

Readiness of the currently English homepage entry routes for localisation. Target audiences, supported locales and fallback policy remain undecided.

  • Scope of internationalisation assessment · supported · level 1 — Authored scope and explicit boundaries.
  • Language and UTF-8 metadata · supported · level 2 — Current generated entry markup; presence checks only.
  • Locale and fallback policy · not-evidenced · level 2 — Choose target audiences, supported locales, defaults and fallback behaviour before claiming readiness.
  • Localisable content evidence · not-evidenced · level 2 — Assess message and content externalisation and supply evidence of locale selection and fallback.
  • Locale behaviour evidence · not-evidenced · level 2 — Exercise locale-sensitive numbers, dates, names, text expansion and text direction as applicable.
  • Language and cultural review · not-evidenced · level 3 — Record linguistic, cultural and typographic review for each promised locale.
  • Locale journeys in use · not-evidenced · level 4 — Observe representative journeys with the intended language and locale audiences.
  • Localisation maintenance · not-evidenced · level 5 — Assign ownership and record translation freshness, fallback and locale regression coverage.

What the current evidence establishes

Language and UTF-8 markers are observed. Supported locale commitments, message/content externalisation, locale selection, fallback, formatting and text direction have not been evidenced by this assessment. Linguistic and cultural review are later obligations.
